message.content: As the context length increased, the model's attention mechanism had to process more tokens simultaneously, which raised computational overhead and memory demands. This resulted in longer inference times and higher latency, especially when the context exceeded the model's typical attention window, forcing it to rely on more distant token relationships and increasing the number of attention heads required. Consequently, throughput (tokens processed per second) decreased, and the model's ability to maintain high accuracy under extended context lengths became more challenging, highlighting the trade‑off between context capacity and inference speed.
